read.instructionDe: Lesen Sie die Karte. Tippen Sie auf ein Wort für seine Bedeutung.
read.instructionEn: Read the menu. Tap a word for its meaning.
read.text:
Café Bremen
Bei uns essen und trinken Sie gut!
Frühstück: Montag bis Samstag, 7 bis 11 Uhr
Frühstück mit Brot und Kaffee: 6 Euro
Suppe oder Salat: 5 Euro
Kuchen: 3 Euro
Tasse Kaffee oder Tee: 2 Euro
Glas Orangensaft: 3 Euro

questions.promptDe: Sie möchten Suppe und eine Tasse Tee. Was kostet das zusammen? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: You would like soup and a cup of tea. How much is that together? Choose the answer.
options: 5 euros.
7 euros.
8 euros.
questions.explanationDe: Auf der Karte steht: Suppe kostet 5 Euro, eine Tasse Tee kostet 2 Euro. Zusammen sind das 7 Euro.
questions.explanationEn: The menu says soup is 5 euros and a cup of tea is 2 euros. Together that is 7 euros.

questions.promptDe: Wann gibt es im Café Frühstück? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: When does the café serve breakfast? Choose the answer.
options: Monday to Saturday, from 7 to 11.
Monday to Friday, from 7 to 11.
Every day, from 7 to 11.
questions.explanationDe: Auf der Karte steht: Frühstück von Montag bis Samstag, 7 bis 11 Uhr. Am Sonntag ist kein Frühstück.
questions.explanationEn: The menu says breakfast is Monday to Saturday, 7 to 11. There is no breakfast on Sunday.

meaning.promptDe: Was möchte Ana? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What would Ana like? Choose the meaning.
options: She is hungry and orders a soup.
She is thirsty and orders a coffee.
She is tired and orders a tea.
meaning.answer: She is thirsty and orders a coffee.

meaning.promptDe: Hat Ana auch Hunger? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: Is Ana hungry too? Choose the meaning.
options: Yes, and she orders cake.
Yes, and she orders soup.
No, she only wants a drink.

meaning.promptDe: Was bestellt Ana noch? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
meaning.promptEn: What else does Ana order? Choose the answer.
options: A cup of tea and a mineral water.
A glass of orange juice and a beer.
A glass of mineral water and an orange juice.
meaning.answer: A glass of mineral water and an orange juice.

meaning.promptDe: Paul hat auch Tee, Bier und Wein. Was sagt Ana? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: Paul also has tea, beer and wine. What does Ana say? Choose the meaning.
options: Yes, please: she orders a glass of wine.
No, thank you: she will eat bread with salad.
No, thank you: she would like the bill.
meaning.answer: No, thank you: she will eat bread with salad.

meaning.promptDe: Was sagt Paul? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What does Paul say? Choose the meaning.
options: The waitress is coming right away with the bread.
The waitress is sorry: there is no bread today.
The bread will take another twenty minutes.
meaning.answer: The waitress is coming right away with the bread.

nextHook.de: Ana steht am Bahnhof und hat viele Fragen: Fährt der Zug nach Österreich? Und was kostet die Fahrkarte?
nextHook.en: Ana is at the station with a lot of questions: does the train go to Austria? And what does the ticket cost?

tasks.promptDe: Sagen Sie die Antwort. Im Café. Der Kellner: „Was möchten Sie trinken?“ Sie: … (Durst!) … (Tee)
tasks.promptEn: In the café, the waiter asks what you would like to drink. Say two sentences: first that you are thirsty, then order tea politely.
tasks.answer: Ich habe Durst. Ich möchte einen Tee, bitte.

tasks.promptEn: You would like salad, but the waiter only mentions soup and cake. Ask him politely whether they have salad too.

tasks.promptDe: Sagen Sie die Antwort. Der Kellner: „Möchten Sie auch Wasser?“ Sie: … (ja!) Der Kellner: „Wir haben auch Wein.“ Sie: … (nein!)
tasks.promptEn: The waiter offers you water: accept politely. Then he offers wine: decline politely.

Ja, ich möchte ein Glas Wasser, bitte.
Ja, ich möchte auch Wasser, bitte.
Ja, ich möchte auch ein Glas Wasser.
Ja, ich möchte auch ein Glas Wasser, bitte.
Nein, danke, ich möchte keinen Wein.

notes: Chunks are the five offer-and-answer pairs (Paul asks or offers, Ana answers); no boundary was in doubt. Each chunk has exactly one learner line, so the say lines (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) were not a choice. None of them is a dictation line (0, 4).

Read text: the café's menu with a price list and breakfast hours. Only Café and essen were missing from the dialogue; Café is the menu's heading and essen stands in the slogan „Bei uns essen und trinken Sie gut!“.
The café has no name anywhere in the course; I called it „Café Bremen“ (Bremen is on DIALOG_NAMES and is Ana's city). Rename it if the story has a name for it.
The prices are mine; the dialogue names none, so nothing can contradict them. The first read question makes the learner add two lines of the menu (5 + 2 euros).
Menu lines drop the article and „ein/eine“ („Tasse Kaffee oder Tee: 2 Euro“), as a printed menu does.

Existing data, dialogue line 7 (zero-based): „Ich esse ein Brot mit Salat.“ is given in English as „I’ll have a sandwich with salad.“ My meaning option says „bread with salad“ to stay with the German the learner hears.

Existing data, dialogue line 9 (zero-based): Ana closes with „Zum Frühstück trinke ich immer eine Tasse Kaffee.“, which does not follow from Paul's line before it; it reads as a line written to carry Frühstück and Tasse. It is the only learner line of the last chunk, so it is the say line, and my meaning question for that chunk asks about Paul's line instead.
Phonetik: MÖCH-te and HÖ-ren are word-stress items; SCHÖN is a one-syllable word and fails the item shape (needs at least two syllables), so the sound stage is pending for L9. Not changed.

PROOF (added 2026-11-14): four tasks, one per can-do, in can-do order. The German prompts are cue dialogues („Sie: …“) without an instruction verb, because RULE 35 holds promptDe to the taught-word horizon; the English twin carries the instruction. The waiter is „Der Kellner“, not „Paul“: a first name invites „…, Paul?“, which the engine does not remove (engine limit 3).

Proof goal 0 (order in the café): two parts, as dialogue line 1 (zero-based): first „Ich habe Durst.“, then the order. Every learner line of this dialogue has two sentences, and a one-part order task would refuse the Lektion’s own line „Ich habe Durst. Ich möchte einen Kaffee, bitte.“ as an extra sentence. So the cue asks for both: „… (Durst!) … (Tee)“. Order: „Ich möchte einen Tee / Tee / eine Tasse Tee / ein Glas Tee“ with or without „, bitte“, also „Und ich möchte …“, „Ich möchte bitte …“, „Ich möchte … trinken“ (the waiter’s question carries the infinitive), the short „Einen Tee, bitte.“ / „Bitte einen Tee.“ and „Ich trinke …“ (Ana orders with „Ich esse …“ in line 7). „ein Tee“ fails (the pool drills einen: extra-a11-l09-07) and a bare „Tee.“ fails. Tea, not the dialogue’s coffee, so the re-teach line 1 has to be adapted.

Proof goal 1 (say that I am hungry or thirsty): two parts, as dialogue line 3: „(Ja,) ich habe (auch) Hunger.“, then the order of soup („Suppe“, „eine Suppe“, „die Suppe“; the same frames, and „Ich esse …“). It proves Hunger; Durst is proven in goal 0. „Ich bin Hunger.“ fails as it should. „Ich bin hungrig.“ cannot be accepted: hungrig is untaught (RULE 35).

Proof goal 2 (ask politely whether there is something): one part, formal. The waiter names soup and cake, the learner would like salad: „Haben Sie (auch) Salat / einen Salat?“, also after „Und “ or „Entschuldigung, “ and before „, bitte“. LIMIT: Ana never asks whether there is something. The form is modelled only by the waiter’s own question in line 2 („Haben Sie auch Hunger?“, the re-teach pointer) and by pool item extra-a11-l09-09 („___ Sie auch Kuchen?“). „Gibt es auch Salat?“ cannot be accepted: RULE 35 reports „Gibt“ as untaught, although the can-do itself and the guided read question („Wann gibt es im Café Frühstück?“) use the word.

Proof goal 3 (accept an offer or decline politely): two parts, formal: accept the water, then decline the wine. Accept: „Ja, bitte.“, „Ja, gern(e).“, „(Ja,) sehr gern(e).“, „Gern(e).“, „Ja, danke.“, „Ja, ein Glas Wasser / ein Wasser / Wasser / ein Glas Mineralwasser, bitte.“, „Ja, ich möchte (auch) (ein Glas) Wasser(, bitte).“ Decline: „Nein, danke.“, „Danke, nein.“, „Nein, danke, ich möchte keinen Wein.“ A bare „Ja.“ or „Nein.“ fails, with the hint „Sagen Sie es höflich.“ Re-teach: dialogue lines 4–7. LIMIT: Ana’s lines 5 and 7 copied whole fail, because each has a second sentence („Und einen Orangensaft.“, „Ich esse ein Brot mit Salat.“); the learner has to keep the first sentence of each.

Proof, register: `register: "formal"` is declared on goals 2 and 3 only. In goals 0 and 1 no form has an address pronoun, and the formal hint („Sagen Sie es höflich.“) would mislead after a miss such as „Ich bin Durst.“

Proof, limits of the engine that hold for every task of this Lektion: (1) A standalone „Entschuldigung!“, „Danke!“ or „Guten Tag!“ before or after the answer counts as an extra sentence and fails. proofTasks() takes the free courtesies from this Lektion’s Wortfeld only (src/lib/lesson/proof.js, `courtesies`), and Danke, Bitte and Entschuldigung are Lektion 1 entries, so here none is free. (2) Any other extra sentence fails as well, also a correct one. (3) A name added to the answer fails („Lena, …“, „…, Paul?“, „Herr Schmidt, …“); the engine removes only a final „, Herr/Frau X“ of a titled speaker of this dialogue. So the prompts use partners without a name. (4) A dot inside a clock time („9.00 Uhr“) splits the answer into two sentences. (5) The notice cannot be a re-teach pointer: its bodyDe fails RULE 35’s word horizon. (6) By microphone the engine scores against the one canonical `answer`, so another accepted form may score low when spoken (read from ProofStage.jsx and answerProof(), not tested).
